tone.target: bright 80s Marshall crunch with slight chorus
tone.profile: bright 80s Marshall crunch with slight chorus
tone.summary: A tight signal chain using an OD boost and UK 45 amp model, paired with the UK Vintage 4x12 cab. Chorus adds the necessary 80s sheen, while Gate 1 controls noise.

rig.name: Bryan Adams - Run To You (Classic Version) - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and maintain tight signal definition.
Provide mid-gain boost and tighten the pick attack for classic 80s rock crunch.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is used as a general mid-boost/overdrive, simulating a Plexi or similar British drive tone.

alternatives.reason: A slightly cleaner alternative if the crunch needs to be less aggressive.

blocks.purpose: Bypass or use for occasional tonal shaping if needed; kept inactive for a straight rock tone.
blocks.gap: The wah effect is not central to the required sound and is best left off.

blocks.purpose: No heavy distortion is required; the Green OD provides sufficient mid-gain crunch.
blocks.gap: The tone requires clean, tight overdrive rather than dedicated fuzz or high gain.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the bright, punchy sound of a Marshall Plexi-style amp head.
blocks.gap: The UK 45 is the closest model to achieve the desired classic British rock tone.

alternatives.reason: A good alternative if a slightly more modern, scooped sound was needed.

blocks.purpose: Provide the classic British rock cabinet sound and frequency response.
Add the required 80s chorus sheen without sounding overly wet or distracting.
Add subtle space and depth to the overall mix without muddying the tight tone.
blocks.gap: A light Room reverb is preferred over Plate or Spring for a natural 80s rock feel.

blocks.purpose: Slightly boost the mids and highs to enhance pick attack and cut through the mix.
blocks.gap: Used for final tonal sculpting, emphasizing the mid-range punch required in 80s rock.
